about: What Validate's conduit rules (E-DERATE, E-VDROP) read off the documents' schedules (Q6338): the wire-length table a set prints to size its branch conductors by length (its title words and its column headers' words, any layout: sizes across with breaker and voltage rows, sizes down with length or voltage columns, or one length range and one size per row), and what a panel schedule's breaker cell must read to be its amps. Common practice on US electrical drawings. Add a project's words here, never in code.

length_table.source: the drawing's own branch-circuit wire-length table: where a set prints one it decides the conductor for a length, ahead of the generic NEC 210.19(A) Informational Note No. 4 calculation

breaker.standard_source: NEC 240.6(A) standard ampere ratings of fuses and inverse time circuit breakers (1 A to 10 A fuses aside)
breaker.over_wire_source: NEC 240.4 and 430.52: a breaker protects its conductor; even a motor circuit's inverse time breaker is at most 250% of its full-load current (up to 400% for starting), so a breaker more than 4 times its own row's conductor ampacity (75 °C column) is no reading of that breaker
